input.statement: Let X and Y be sets of the same universe with |Y| < |X|. Any observation map h:X→Y takes the same value on two distinct inputs.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: Instantiate Objects=X, Readings=Y, read=h; all hypotheses are identical.

input.statement: Let finite sets A,B,C satisfy |C|≤|B|<|A|. For maps f:A→B and g:B→C, distinct a,a′ satisfy g(f(a))=g(f(a′)).

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: First use transitivity to derive |C|<|A|, then apply the source theorem to g∘f. Both cardinal premises form one joint premise set.

input.statement: Let nonempty finite sets X,Y satisfy |Y|≤|X|. Every h:X→Y takes equal values at two distinct inputs.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: Take X=Y={0} and h the identity. There are no two distinct inputs. The strict inequality cannot be dropped.

input.statement: In a commutative ring R let p²=p+1, q²=q+1, p+q=1 and pq=−1; let m be a nonnegative integer. For u_j=a p^j+b q^j, u_(m+1)²−u_(m+1)u_m−u_m²=−5ab(−1)^m.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: Rename φ=p, ψ=q, A=a, B=b, K=m. All four hypotheses remain.

input.statement: In a commutative ring R let p²=p+1, q²=q+1, p+q=1 and pq=−1; let m be a nonnegative integer. For v_j=p^j−q^j, v_(m+1)²−v_(m+1)v_m−v_m²=5(−1)^m.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: Substitute A=1 and B=−1 in the source, then normalize −5·1·(−1)=5.

input.statement: For any integers p,q,a,b and m≥0, u_j=a p^j+b q^j satisfies u_(m+1)²−u_(m+1)u_m−u_m²=−5ab(−1)^m.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: p=q=0, a=b=1, m=1 gives left side 0 and right side 5.

input.statement: For real symmetric idempotent N×N matrices P_1,…,P_n, let M be their mean and S the average of all n! ordered products. For every n≥1,N, M^n−S is positive semidefinite.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: The frozen result refutes exactly this universal claim at n=N=3. With v_i=2e_i−(1,1,1), P_i=v_i v_iᵀ/3 and z=(1,1,1), zᵀ(M³−S)z=−8/243. This labels the formal claim, not an independently checked bibliographic priority assertion.

input.statement: For any three orthogonal projections E,F,G on R³, ((E+F+G)/3)^3−(EFG+EGF+FEG+FGE+GEF+GFE)/6 is positive semidefinite.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: The same three rank-one real symmetric projections satisfy all hypotheses; ordering conventions give the same symmetric average.

input.statement: For real symmetric idempotent N×N matrices P_1,…,P_n, let M be their mean and S the average of all n! ordered products. Restrict to n=2. The cited n=3 counterexample proves that M²−S fails to be positive semidefinite for some P_1,P_2.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: For two symmetric projections, M²−S=(P_1−P_2)²/4, which is positive semidefinite. An n=3 refutation cannot be reused as an n=2 counterexample.

input.statement: Use the source finite independent listing model: A,Y finite, q:A×Y→R cell weights, f:Y→Y, w(s) the product of all |A|² cell weights, C(s) the number of rows equal to the f-twisted diagonal. Define T_k=Σ_{C(s)≥k}w(s) and B_k=Σ_s binom(C(s),k)w(s). If all q(a,y)≥0, then T_k≤B_k for every natural k.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: The source identifies its subset-capture sum with B_k. Pointwise 1_{C≥k}≤binom(C,k), and w≥0 preserves the inequality under summation.

input.statement: Use the source finite independent listing model: A,Y finite, q:A×Y→R cell weights, f:Y→Y, w(s) the product of all |A|² cell weights, C(s) the number of rows equal to the f-twisted diagonal. Define T_k=Σ_{C(s)≥k}w(s) and B_k=Σ_s binom(C(s),k)w(s). If all q(a,y)≥0, then B_k−k B_(k+1)≤T_k≤B_k.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: Combine the lower and upper source theorems, with the same q,f,k and nonnegative weights. Neither theorem by itself proves both bounds.

input.statement: Use the source finite independent listing model: A,Y finite, q:A×Y→R cell weights, f:Y→Y, w(s) the product of all |A|² cell weights, C(s) the number of rows equal to the f-twisted diagonal. Define T_k=Σ_{C(s)≥k}w(s) and B_k=Σ_s binom(C(s),k)w(s). With arbitrary signed real q, T_1≤B_1.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: Let |A|=3, Y a singleton, f its identity and every cell weight −1. The unique sample has weight (−1)^9=−1 and C=3, giving T_1=−1 and B_1=−3.

input.statement: For a finite complex vector v, put ρ=vv*. If v*v=1, then for every matrix H, ρ²=ρ and ρHρ=Tr(Hρ)ρ.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: Apply pure_state_handshake to v,H and replace its middle scalar by the third conjunct. Both conjuncts are used.

input.statement: For a finite complex vector v, put ρ=vv*. For arbitrary v, ρ²=ρ.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: In dimension one with v=2, ρ=4 and ρ²=16. Normalization is necessary for this conclusion.

input.statement: For a finite complex vector v, put ρ=vv*. For arbitrary v and every matrix H, ρHρ=(v*Hv)ρ, without a normalization hypothesis.

label.scope: selected published premises; no global novelty label
label.argument: The source second-conjunct proof expands finite sums and never uses hv; entrywise (vv*Hvv*)_ij=v_i(Σ_kl conjugate(v_k)H_kl v_l)conjugate(v_j). This is an algebraically checked relation, not a bind-only certificate obtained by applying the whole source theorem.

label.argument: All parameters, the canonical normalization, the monotonicity assumptions and the closed right-tail condition coincide with the source.

label.argument: a_0=0, strict increase and monotonicity of constant b hold. The tail condition specializes to t≥−2n.

label.argument: Take a_j=j, b_j=j, n=1 and t=−2. Then q_0=1, q_1=−2, q_2=5/2, so q_1²−2q_0q_2=−1. All remaining assumptions hold.
